why: Source: two profits, two per-item divisions, percentage change, pick the option (6 steps); question: the same two profits, two per-wash divisions, percentage change and pick (6 steps), with the same profit-margin distractor row.

Source: five labelled bar-pair differences and percentage falls, then order them against the options (about 6 steps); question: the same five percentage falls from a labelled two-series bar chart and the same ordering (about 6 steps).

Source: hours for each period from FTE x monthly hours, hours-to-minutes conversion, two divisions, difference (5 steps); question: the same FTE-hours, minutes conversion, two divisions and difference (5 steps).

Source: five ratios of labelled bars from two charts restricted to Regions A-E, then a ranking with one close call (about 6 steps); question: five ratios for Branches A-E from two labelled charts and a ranking with one close call (about 6 steps).

Source: baseline minutes per unit, then for each of four options read the FTE step off an unlabelled step chart, compute minutes per unit and compare, spotting the threshold crossing (about 9 steps); question: the same baseline, four step-chart readings, four minutes-per-unit calculations and the same threshold trap (about 9 steps).

Source: one-time visitors = people x fraction, divide by total visits avoiding the divide-by-people trap (3 steps); question: the same multiplication, division by visits and visits-not-people trap (3 steps).

Source: four statements checked on an unlabelled three-line indexed chart (share of hourly staff over two weeks, point rises, proportionality of a move, the base-week trap) (about 6 steps); question: the same four statement types on the same kind of unlabelled indexed chart (about 6 steps).
Source: locate the right pie, sum three slices, multiply by the respondent share (3 steps); question: locate the right pie among four, sum three slices, multiply by 26% (3 steps).

Source: annual maintenance and electricity cost for each model (with cents-to-dollars conversion), annual saving, times three years (about 5 steps); question: the same servicing and electricity costs, conversion, saving and three-year payback (about 5 steps), with servicing now a small offsetting cost rather than a saving.

Source: total each series and the overall total, then test four percentage-threshold statements (about 6 steps); question: the same three totals from a labelled stacked bar and four threshold checks (about 6 steps).
